chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Faddal, from one who narrated to him, from Sa'd ibn Tarif, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The people used to die arbitrarily. So when the era of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) came, he said: 'O my Lord! Appoint for death a cause by which the deceased shall be rewarded and by which the bereaved shall be consoled.'
He said: So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down serious illness (al-mum), which is pleurisy (al-birsam). Then He sent down the cure after it.

key_terms.الْبِرْسَام: Pleurisy or inflammation of the pleural cavity (chest); a grave illness historically associated with high mortality
key_terms.الْمُوم: A serious illness involving high fever; identified in the text with al-birsam (pleurisy/inflammation of the chest cavity)
key_terms.عِلَّة: Cause, reason, or illness; here used in both senses — a medical cause for death and a purpose/rationale for the dying process
key_terms.يَعْتَبِطُونَ: To die suddenly without prior illness; arbitrary death without evident cause — a term from classical Arabic for unexpected death of the young and healthy
key_terms.يُؤْجَر: To be rewarded (passive form); the patient endurance of illness was understood to earn divine recompense for the believer
key_terms.يُسَلَّى: To be consoled/comforted; the illness and its visible signs allow the bereaved to mentally prepare for loss

ai.seo_question: Why did Allah ordain illness before death according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) narrates a cosmological account of how illness came to precede death. Before the time of Ibrahim (AS), people would die without any apparent cause — what classical scholars called 'al-itibat,' sudden or arbitrary death without illness. The Prophet Ibrahim (AS) petitioned Allah that death be preceded by illness so that the dying person could earn divine reward through patience in suffering, and the survivors could prepare themselves for their loss. In response, Allah sent down al-mum (serious fever/pleurisy) followed by its treatment, establishing the pattern of illness preceding death as a mercy for both the dying and the living.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from the one who narrated it, from Sa’ad Bin Tareyf, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The people used to die arbitrarily. So when it was the era of Ibrahim<sup>as</sup>, he<sup>as</sup> said: ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! Make a cause to be for the death for the deceased to be Recompensed by and for the affected ones to be consoled by’.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Sent down serious illness, and it is the pleurisy. Then He<sup>azwj</sup> Sent down the cure after it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn Faddal from those who narrated to him from Sa‘d ibn Tarif who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

People would just drop dead. Ibrahim (Abraham), ‘Alayhi al Salam, in his time pleaded before Allah to create a cause for death so the dying person receives rewards and the grieving people find solace.
Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, then sent al-Mum, which is a kind of fever causing hallucination and thereafter He sent medicine.’”
